# Mixed-width rounding transitions

**2026-09-29 correction:** The coupled eight-twip edge allowance and constrained
rounding rule now pass these native controls. The prior expected failures have
been removed without relaxing the 0.2pt geometry gate. Notes below describing
pending fixes or failed candidates are historical evidence against the parent
implementation (db793e48); they are superseded by this result. Automatic cells
with unresolved grid subdivisions remain outside the new rounding rule.


Original handcrafted OOXML control, generated by
`python tools/mixed_width_rounding_fixture.py` from our own committed
`mixed-cell-width-content/control.docx`. No corpus artwork or font files.
The 42 cases vary only table/footer preferred width, 5990 through 6010 twips,
in paired body-only and all-cell noWrap groups. All other cell content,
margins, Arial 9pt runs, saved grid and preferences remain identical.

`powershell.exe -NoProfile -File tools/record_mixed_width_rounding.ps1` reproduces
the native width measurements using the installed reference-opening helper. It
uses the retained PDF only for provenance hashing; capture the PDF separately
with the reference automation API's ExportAsFixedFormat (format 17), without saving the DOCX.

The reference application opened the source. After Repaginate, each third-row
cell's Width was read through COM and converted from points to twips; the reference application
exported the PDF without saving the source. `reference.json` hash-binds
source, cases and native PDF. The source passes all three applicable XSD parts.

The body-only controls have automatic widths 436/436 at 6001, 437/437 at
6002, then 436/436 at 6003. All-cell controls retain 437/437 and allow totals
one twip beyond the requested width at 5999, 6000, 6001 and 6003. This disproves
a constant automatic-column bias and a globally exact preferred-width total.
The ordinary round-each-column/remainder policy matches 34 of 42 complete
native grids. Simply flooring automatic columns repairs some old cases but
regresses others; it is not a renderer candidate.

These are allocation observations, not a completed layout correction. No
browser fidelity tolerance or production rule is changed. The existing
case-2 expected failure remains. Next work must explain the constraint-driven
rounding transitions while retaining existing fixed and percentage grids.
Relevant ECMA-376 Part 1 clauses: 17.4.29, 17.4.49, 17.4.63, 17.4.71 and
17.18.87. The layout guidance allows alternative algorithms; this does not
establish a normative specification conflict.
